title: 178. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Factoring by Grouping
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Factoring a Four-Term Polynomial by Grouping
questions.learningObjective: Factor a four-term polynomial by grouping terms with a common binomial factor.
questions.question: Factor \(x^3+2x^2+3x+6\) by grouping.
questions.explanation:
Group the first two terms and the last two terms, then factor out the common binomial \((x+2)\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
(x^3+2x^2)+(3x+6) &= x^2(x+2)+3(x+2)\\
&= (x+2)(x^2+3)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((x+2)(x^2+3)\).
questions.hint: Group the first two terms and the last two terms, then look for a common binomial factor.

questions.learningObjective: Factor a four-term polynomial by grouping and identifying a common binomial factor.
questions.question: Factor \(x^3-3x^2+4x-12\) by grouping.
questions.explanation:
Group the terms and factor each group. The common binomial factor is \((x-3)\), so:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(x^3-3x^2)+(4x-12) &= x^2(x-3)+4(x-3)\\
&= (x-3)(x^2+4)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((x-3)(x^2+4)\).
questions.hint: Factor each pair of terms separately, then factor out the repeated binomial.

questions.concept: Factoring by Grouping with a Leading Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Factor a four-term polynomial by grouping when one group has a leading coefficient.
questions.question: Factor \(2x^3+6x^2+x+3\) by grouping.
questions.explanation:
Group the terms, then factor out the common binomial \((x+3)\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2x^3+6x^2)+(x+3) &= 2x^2(x+3)+1(x+3)\\
&= (x+3)(2x^2+1)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((x+3)(2x^2+1)\).
questions.hint: After grouping, check whether both groups share the same binomial factor.

questions.concept: Factoring by Grouping with a Negative Binomial Factor
questions.learningObjective: Factor a four-term polynomial by grouping and handling a negative common factor.
questions.question: Factor \(3x^3-15x^2-2x+10\) by grouping.
questions.explanation:
Group the terms, then factor out the common binomial \((x-5)\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
(3x^3-15x^2)+(-2x+10) &= 3x^2(x-5)-2(x-5)\\
&= (x-5)(3x^2-2)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((x-5)(3x^2-2)\).
questions.hint: In the second group, factor out \(-2\) so that the binomial factor matches the first group.

questions.concept: Factoring by Grouping with a Negative Second Group
questions.learningObjective: Factor a four-term polynomial by grouping when a negative factor must be taken out of the second group.
questions.question: Factor \(6x^3+4x^2-9x-6\) by grouping.
questions.explanation:
Group the terms, then factor out the common binomial \((3x+2)\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
(6x^3+4x^2)+(-9x-6) &= 2x^2(3x+2)-3(3x+2)\\
&= (3x+2)(2x^2-3)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((3x+2)(2x^2-3)\).
questions.hint: Choose the signs in the second group so that the common binomial matches.

questions.concept: Factoring by Grouping with a Leading Coefficient and Negative Terms
questions.learningObjective: Factor a four-term polynomial by grouping when a negative factor is taken out of the second group.
questions.question: Factor \(4x^3+8x^2-3x-6\) by grouping.
questions.explanation:
Group the terms, then factor out the common binomial \((x+2)\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
(4x^3+8x^2)+(-3x-6) &= 4x^2(x+2)-3(x+2)\\
&= (x+2)(4x^2-3)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((x+2)(4x^2-3)\).
questions.hint: Factor each pair of terms, then look for the repeated binomial factor.

questions.concept: Factoring by Grouping After Removing a Common Monomial
questions.learningObjective: Factor a polynomial by first removing a common monomial and then grouping.
questions.question: Factor \(2x^4+6x^3+4x^2+12x\) completely.
questions.explanation:
First factor out the common monomial \(2x\), then group the polynomial inside the parentheses. Thus:
\[
\begin{aligned}
2x^4+6x^3+4x^2+12x &= 2x(x^3+3x^2+2x+6)\\
x^3+3x^2+2x+6 &= x^2(x+3)+2(x+3)\\
&= (x+3)(x^2+2)\\
2x^4+6x^3+4x^2+12x &= 2x(x+3)(x^2+2)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the complete factorization is \(2x(x+3)(x^2+2)\).
questions.hint: Always remove the greatest common monomial factor first, then group the remaining polynomial.

questions.concept: Factoring by Grouping with Two Variables
questions.learningObjective: Factor a four-term polynomial with two variables by grouping.
questions.question: Factor \(3a^2b-6a^2-4b+8\) by grouping.
questions.explanation:
Group the terms, then factor out the common binomial \((b-2)\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
(3a^2b-6a^2)+(-4b+8) &= 3a^2(b-2)-4(b-2)\\
&= (b-2)(3a^2-4)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((b-2)(3a^2-4)\).
questions.hint: Group terms that share a common variable or constant factor, then factor out the repeated binomial.

questions.concept: Factoring by Grouping with a Sign Change
questions.learningObjective: Factor a four-term polynomial by grouping after factoring out a negative number.
questions.question: Factor \(2x^3-3x^2-4x+6\) by grouping.
questions.explanation:
Group the terms, then factor out the common binomial \((2x-3)\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2x^3-3x^2)+(-4x+6) &= x^2(2x-3)-2(2x-3)\\
&= (2x-3)(x^2-2)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((2x-3)(x^2-2)\).
questions.hint: In the second group, factoring out \(-2\) makes the binomial factor match the first group.

questions.concept: Factoring by Grouping with a Common Binomial Factor
questions.learningObjective: Factor a four-term polynomial by grouping and extracting the common binomial factor.
questions.question: Factor \(6x^3-9x^2+4x-6\) by grouping.
questions.explanation:
Group the terms, then factor out the common binomial \((2x-3)\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
(6x^3-9x^2)+(4x-6) &= 3x^2(2x-3)+2(2x-3)\\
&= (2x-3)(3x^2+2)
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, the correct factorization is \((2x-3)(3x^2+2)\).
questions.hint: Group the first two terms and the last two terms, then factor out the repeated binomial.
